Dispatch notes for the executing seat:
- **Premise-first, in this order**: ① measure whether a NON-admin file owner (or any caller who can reference the row) can `PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_file/` on `mime_type`/`size`. If FLS/RLS already blocks it ⇒ close with the measurement as evidence (`premise_still_valid: false` + no PR is a good run — the admin-path half is expected privilege, per the card itself). ② Only if the non-admin PATCH lands: fix by making those columns system-managed/immutable post-commit (or server-side re-derive at check time) — do not widen anything.
- **Clause-② `yes` if phase ② runs**: making previously-writable columns immutable narrows accepted writes on a published data surface. Contract-review tier applies to that half.
- The broader content-vs-declaration boundary (no magic-byte sniffing) is explicitly out of scope here — the card says it is tracked separately; do not fold it in.
- Reproduction withheld per the disclosure carve-out (QA session #10663).

Size/model suggestion: M, opus (measurement + possible tightening).

Claim: dispatched as **measurement-only**. No code change is authorised by this dispatch.

- session: user-29 [974948]
- branch: `claude/issue-10702-sysfile-metadata-mutability`
- worktree: `../objectstack-10702`
- Clause-②: **not applicable at this tier** — this dispatch changes no code. If the measurement comes back positive, the fix is a separate card and it *will* be Clause-②.
- serial constraint: `service-storage` / `sys_file` metadata surface. Freed by #10951 (merged). No other services card holds it.

## Why measurement-only, and not a fix

The card's own split is the reason. What is **proven** is the seeded platform admin nulling `mime_type`/`size` — and the card says so itself: *"As admin this is expected privilege, not a hole."* What is **open** is the only half that decides whether a defect exists at all:

> whether a **non-admin file owner** (or any caller who can reference the row) can PATCH those columns … If RLS/FLS blocks the non-admin PATCH, this is a non-issue.

Dispatching a repair now would be building a fix for a defect nobody has shown exists. The answer to that one question is the entire deliverable.

## The one question

Under RLS/FLS as shipped, can a **non-admin** caller — specifically a file owner, and separately any authenticated caller who can reference the row — succeed at `PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_file/<id>` writing `mime_type` and/or `size`?

Answer it **both directions**, and make the negative provable:

- A refusal must be shown to be a *refusal*, with its ADR-0112 envelope — assert `code` **AND** `status` (ADR-0112), not status alone. A `200` carrying an empty result is not a refusal, and this lane has been bitten by exactly that shape (#10954: `get-session` answers `200` for anonymous).
- A success must be shown to actually persist — read the row back, do not trust the write's response.
- **Positive control on the same persona and corpus**: prove the non-admin CAN write something on that row (or that the row is reachable at all), so a refusal is a refusal and not a broken fixture, a missing row, or a mis-seeded persona. Without it, a clean "denied" is indistinguishable from "the test never reached the endpoint".
- ⛔ #3807 applies: `null` is not "not mine". Do not read a null/absent result as a denial.

## ⛔ Disclosure discipline — binding

This card is under the auth/authz carve-out. The full reproduction stays in QA session **#10663** and must not be restated.

- **No reproduction recipe** in the PR body, the card, any commit message, or any comment — not the request shapes, not the persona-seeding steps, not the field values that trigger it.
- Report the **verdict and the mechanism**, not the path to it. "A non-admin file owner can/cannot persist `mime_type` on their own row; the control that decides it is X" is the shape to aim for.
- If you need the withheld detail, ask on #10663 rather than reconstructing and publishing it.

## Outcomes and what each means

| measurement | what you file |
|---|---|
| non-admin PATCH **refused** with a real envelope, positive control green | report it; recommend this card be **closed as a non-issue**, with the control named. Do not close it yourself. |
| non-admin PATCH **succeeds** | this is an authz-adjacent defect. Report `needs_decision` with the measurement. Do **not** fix it here — the fix (immutable-post-commit vs. server-side re-derivation at check time, per the card's own two directions) is a permission-boundary change and a separate Clause-② card. |
| you cannot reach a verdict | say so with the measurement that blocked you. A gate or harness that refuses is **NOT MEASURED**, never a pass. |

## Standing instrument traps (all measured in this repo)

- A gate's refusal (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET … Nothing was checked`) is NOT MEASURED, not green.
- An unwired script name exits **254 `Command not found`** and reads GREEN through a pipe.
- Capture exit codes **before** any pipe (`cmd > file 2>&1; EXIT=$?`), never after a `tail`.
- Do not report a grep hit count as a fact count — this lane has been wrong that way four times today.
- Worktree-first, per repo. **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo and a `pop` reports success while taking another agent's work.

## Refs

QA #10663 (parent; holds the withheld reproduction) · #10951 (freed this surface) · #3807 · ADR-0112

PM review of the measurement run. Label moved to `needs-user-decision`, assignee cleared, `pm:dispatched` dropped — this is no longer a dispatchable card.

## The verdict, and why it does not close this card

The open half is answered: **as shipped, a non-admin cannot write `sys_file.mime_type`/`size` through the data API.** Both personas — the owner and a non-owner — got `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, and a system-context read-back confirmed the stored values were unchanged.

A shallow reading stops there and closes this as a non-issue. The measurement does not support that, and the reason is the finding:

> the control is that the explicit-allow platform baseline (`member_default`, #5491) **NAMES no `sys_file` grant**

The refusal is object-level RBAC declining to grant `update` on `sys_file` to `[everyone]`. It is **not** a protection of those two columns. The second posture proves it: with an app-authored wildcard object grant union-merged onto the same baseline, **both** non-admin personas got `200` and the null-metadata write **persisted** — the non-owner included, so neither ownership nor the ownership-floor RLS caught it.

So the accept/maxSize re-check — a declared security property — reads its inputs from a row defended by an **absence**, and any app that grants edit on `sys_file` hands a non-admin the bypass.

## Independently confirmed, by content, on `origin/main` @ `047ac86ee`

I re-derived the three load-bearing structural claims rather than accepting them:

| claim | check | result |
|---|---|---|
| `sys_file` declares no `managedBy` bucket | grep the object source | **no match** — and the positive control shows `managedBy` IS in use on sibling platform objects (`sys-attachment`, `sys-email`, `sys-job-queue`, `sys-job`, `sys-import-job`, `sys-email-template`, `sys-job-run`, 1 each), so the absence is real and not a broken pattern |
| `mime_type`/`size` are not readonly | read `system-file.object.ts` | `mime_type` at `:50`, `size` at `:54` — **neither carries `readonly`** — while `:35` shows another field on the same object does. The mechanism is live on this very object and simply does not cover these two |
| the baseline names no `sys_file` grant | attempted static read | ⚠️ **I did not confirm this statically** — `app-default-permission-set.ts` declares the mechanism (`PLATFORM_BASELINE_PERMISSION_SET = 'member_default'`) and names no `sys_*` object at all, so it is not the grant list. The dev's evidence is the runtime refusal log naming the object and the position, which is stronger than a static read; I am recording that I relied on theirs here rather than reproducing it |

The file's own comment at `:104` corroborates the mechanism independently: *"stayed invisible until #5491 removed `member_default`'s `'*'` wildcard"* — the same explicit-allow transition the measurement leans on.

## Two things this run did that are worth naming

**The instrument was disqualified before the conclusion was.** The first run truncated a response body before parsing it and died on a `SyntaxError`. The harness was corrected — not the conclusion reported around it.

**The refusal was proved to be a refusal.** The seeded admin got `200` on the **same row and the same two columns**, and the change persisted. That is what separates "the members were denied" from "the request never reached the endpoint" — the failure mode this lane has been bitten by (#10954: `get-session` answers `200` for anonymous).

## ⛔ Maintainer decision — not mine to make

The dev's framing is right and I am not overriding it:

> my measurement cannot settle whether an app-revocable grant is an acceptable control for a platform security input

The rule is that a security **tightening** is not a maintainer floor, so option B is technically dispatchable by this seat. I am not dispatching it, because B does not merely tighten a check — it **removes an affordance from app authors**, changing what an app is permitted to grant. That is a platform posture call, not a lane call.

| | option | cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | close as a non-issue on the measured refusal, naming the control | zero work; defensible today; leaves the property defended by an absence |
| **B** | re-scope to a Clause-② card: mark `sys_file` engine-owned (ADR-0103 `managedBy`) or mark the two columns readonly/system-managed post-commit | narrows a write affordance with **no measured consumer** — the upload path stamps these columns and no shipped app grants the object |
| **C** | close, and file a narrower follow-up: re-derive the metadata server-side at check time instead of trusting the stored row | adds a derivation path on the upload/check hot path |
| **D** | close as non-issue **plus** a pin locking in the measured refusal, so a future baseline change granting `sys_file` writes to members turns a gate red | cheap; rider on any of the above |

**My recommendation: B, with D as a rider** — same as the dev's, reached independently from the structural reads above. The deciding fact for me is the `managedBy` absence sitting next to seven siblings that declare it: `sys_file` is not deliberately in the writable bucket, it is in it by omission, and ADR-0103's engine-owned bucket exists precisely to end that shape. D is worth its cost regardless of which option wins, because the control today is an absence and an absence has no gate.

Say the word and I dispatch B immediately — no further consultation needed.

## Housekeeping

No product code was changed, no PR opened, no changeset. The probe branch carries no commits. ⛔ The harness is **not** committed: under the auth/authz carve-out it *is* the reproduction. If a pin is wanted (option D), it must be authored as a refusal pin, not as the harness.

Full reproduction remains in QA session #10663.

## Closing per the ruling's pre-agreed routing — and recording the half the routing did not cover

⚠️ **The authorized measurement was already complete when the ruling landed.** The ruling (13:50Z) authorizes 「查」 — the non-admin measurement only. That measurement ran at **03:10Z** and its report is on this card. So nothing was dispatched; the routing is simply applied to a result that already existed.

**Routing precondition: met.** RLS/FLS blocks the PATCH.

| persona | verdict |
|---|---|
| file owner (`owner_id` server-stamped to them) | `403` `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `persisted: false` — value write **and** null write |
| authenticated non-owner | identical |
| **contrast control**: seeded platform admin, **same row, same two columns** | `200`, change persisted |

That last row is what makes the 403 a **refusal** rather than a request that never reached the endpoint — the failure shape this lane was bitten by on #10954, where `get-session` answered `200` for anonymous. Positive controls on the same personas and route family confirmed each could create (201) and update (200) an app-object record.

⇒ **Closed as a non-issue, per the routing.** `pm:queue` and the assignee cleared.

## ⛔ The reading, in full — because "close **with the reading**" is what the ruling says

The refusal is **object-level RBAC**, not a protection of these two columns. The server's own log names the mechanism:

> `Access denied: operation 'update' on object 'sys_file' is not permitted for positions [everyone]`

The control is that the explicit-allow platform baseline (`member_default`, #5491) **names no `sys_file` grant**. Verified structurally, by content, independently of the run:

- `sys_file` declares **no `managedBy` bucket** — and the positive control shows seven sibling platform objects **do** declare one (`sys-attachment`, `sys-email`, `sys-job-queue`, `sys-job`, `sys-import-job`, `sys-email-template`, `sys-job-run`). So it sits in the writable `platform` bucket **by omission, not by decision**.
- `mime_type` (`:50`) and `size` (`:54`) carry **no `readonly`**, while `:35` on the same object does — the mechanism is live on this very row and simply does not cover these two.

**The half the binary routing did not anticipate**: with an app-authored wildcard object grant union-merged onto the same baseline, **both** non-admin personas got `200` and the write **persisted** on system read-back — the non-owner included, so neither ownership nor the ownership-floor RLS caught it.

So the accept/maxSize re-check — a declared security property — reads its inputs from a row whose only defence is **an absence**. Nothing shipped opens it today (the showcase app's permission sets contain no wildcard and no `sys_file` grant), which is why closing is correct. But an absence has no gate, and the next app profile that grants edit on `sys_file` re-opens it silently.

## What I am doing about that, and what I am not

⛔ **Not** dispatching option B (mark `sys_file` engine-owned, or the columns readonly post-commit). The ruling authorized the measurement, not the fix, and B removes an affordance from **app authors** — a platform posture call, not a lane call. It stays unmade.

✅ **Filing option D as its own unassigned card** — a pin locking in the measured refusal, so a future baseline change granting `sys_file` writes to members turns a gate **red** instead of shipping quietly. D changes no behaviour; it converts "defended by an absence" into "defended by a gate", and it is the one thing that is correct under **every** disposition of B. Filed at **#11074**, ungraded, for triage.

⚠️ The pin must be authored as a **refusal pin**, not as the harness — the harness *is* the reproduction and was deliberately never committed, under the auth/authz carve-out. Full reproduction remains in QA session #10663.

## One process note

This is the second card today where a batch ruling arrived after the work it authorizes had already been done. Not a problem here — the routing was binary and the answer was in hand — but worth noting that the decision inbox and the dispatch loop can drift out of step by several hours, and a ruling that reads as "go measure" may be describing a measurement already on the card.
